title: incident-bot: add SLO hint scoring & runbook linking helpers for on-call diagnostics
author: Ava Patel
commits: refactor(incident-bot): split diagnostics pipeline and introduce hint scoring (a1b2c3d)
feat(slo-toolkit): add SLO hint scoring utilities and weights config (d4e5f6g)
feat(runbooks): runbook linking helper and fuzzy matching for runbook titles (h7i8j9k)
chore(tests): add unit + integration tests for hint scoring and linking (l0m1n2o)
docs: document on-call helpers and migration notes (p3q4r5s)
description:
Motivation:
The on-call flow frequently surfaces noisy runbook suggestions and low-utility diagnostics. We want the incident-bot to surface higher-quality runbooks and to provide explicit SLO-related hints to on-call responders. This PR adds a SLO hint scoring utility, runbook-linking helpers, and telemetry to measure effectiveness.

Summary of changes:
- Add libs/slo-toolkit/src/hints/score_utils.py: lightweight, configurable scoring for candidate hints derived from SLO/alert context. Scores are a weighted sum of signal types (symptom-match, latency-regression, recent-change, service-impact) where weights are pluggable via config.
- Add services/incident-bot/src/diagnostics/hint_scoring.py: wrapper that normalizes signals from incident context and calls the scoring utilities. Provides top-N hints and a confidence score used for UI ranking.
- Add services/incident-bot/src/diagnostics/runbook_linker.py: fuzzy title matching + tag-based linking for runbooks; includes fallbacks when exact matches are not found and generates a confidence metric.
- Instrument telemetry: infra/telemetry/metrics.yaml adds metrics for hint_score_distribution, runbook_link_success, and runbook_click_through.
- Add on-call helpers: services/incident-bot/handlers/oncall_helpers.py exposes endpoints used by the UI to fetch scored hints and runbook links.
- Tests: unit and integration tests for scoring, linking, and handler responses.
- Docs and examples: docs/oncall/incident-bot-runbook-helpers.md plus quickstart example.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Scoring is intentionally heuristic and deterministic (no model or heavy ML) to keep latency sub-50ms. We selected a weighted-sum approach to make behavior auditable and allow ops to tune weights quickly.
- Runbook linking uses a combination of tag intersection and fuzzy title matching (token-set ratio) to maximize precision; we avoid broad semantic embeddings to reduce dependency surface for on-call latency.
- Confidence metrics are conservative; if confidence < 0.4 we surface the runbook as "suggested" rather than primary.

Testing and validation:
- Added unit tests covering edge cases (missing metadata, multiple candidate runbooks, identical scores).
- Integration tests simulate an alert payload and assert top-3 hint ordering and runbook link presence.
- Ran canary in staging for 72 hours: runbook_link_success increased by 18% and runbook_click_through up 9% on a sampled set of pages.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind incident-bot runtime flag (deploy/k8s/incident-bot-configmap.yaml).
- Default weights set conservatively; ops can tweak via ConfigMap without redeploy.
- Gradual rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours with monitoring on hint_score_distribution and runbook_link_success.

Rollback:
- Flip the runtime flag off to restore previous behavior. Config changes are non-breaking.

Security and privacy:
- No new sensitive data is persisted. Runbook metadata is internal. Telemetry counts are coarse-grained and do not include raw alert payloads.

Migration notes:
- No migration needed for existing runbooks. Ops may want to tune weights for services with many similarly-named runbooks.
